notes:
Account background: Emberfield builds AI-first route optimization and real-time dispatch for last-mile logistics. Heavy token volumes due to telemetry aggregation + conversational driver assist. Primary ask is enterprise Dedicated capacity with multi-region failover and predictable throughput for peak windows.

Technical requirements / asks (shorthand):
- Target steady-state throughput: ~2k-3k tokens/sec aggregate across the platform; peak bursts up to 8k tokens/sec for short windows (5–15 min).
- Latency SLO: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms for generation endpoints tied to driver-facing chat.
- Workloads: chat (low-latency), embeddings for vector search, reranking for candidate lists.
- Models: prefer open Llama-family 70B / 13B variants quantized; willing to consider Llama-2-Chat/Redwood-curated variants. Also expressed interest in H100-class perf for heavy reranking batches.
- Hardware ask: reserved GPU pool design that includes mix of H100 (or equivalent) and A100 80GB for memory-heavy rerank jobs; templated pool sizing per region.
- Multi-region plan: primary region NA-West (us-west-2-like), failover NA-East and EU-West. Want cross-region reserved headroom to be >=30% of peak to guarantee failover without queueing.
- Availability target: 99.95% platform plus clear outage runbooks; require canary and automatic fallback to lower-cost variants under pressure.
- KV cache considerations: long-tail sequences and cold-starts caused p99 spikes in POC — asking for warmup strategies, cross-AZ sticky routing and guarantee of warm cache node counts per tenant.

Procurement / commercial:
- Emberfield prefers a reserved capacity model (monthly commit) but wants flexibility for burst capacity in cloud during seasonal peaks. Looking for pricing tiers: baseline reserved + burst pool + per-token overage.
- Legal wants explicit p99 latency crediting in SLA; finance concerned about minimum commit length (12 vs 24 months).

Open technical questions (from 2026-02-04 call):
- How will reserved headroom be allocated across regions vs. held centrally? Can we reserve an elastic buffer that moves on failover?
- How is KV cache migrated/rehydrated during failover without large spike in latency?
- Formal throughput guarantees for mixed-model workloads (chat + rerank + embeddings) — need baseline testing methodology and acceptance criteria.

Action items / next steps (shorthand):
- Redwood (Maya + Arjun) to produce a detailed reserved GPU pool plan showing per-region node counts, AZ spread, expected utilization profiles, and failover capacity assumptions by 2026-02-21.
- Draft SLA with p99 language and credit structure; add clause for failover verification and joint runbook. Target delivery 2026-02-21.
- Schedule technical POC to validate warm-cache strategies and cross-AZ routing (two-week focused test) w/ infra team by 2026-02-24.
- Emberfield to provide traffic shape CSVs and peak window calendar.

Stated quotes / call excerpts:
- "We can’t have drivers wait; p99 spikes cost tens of thousands in missed deliveries." — Head of Platform (call 2026-01-28).
- "If you can show us a plan that guarantees failover without >30% latency degradation, procurement will be comfortable with a 12–18 month reserved commit." — CTO (email 2026-02-09).

Blockers summary: procurement timeline (~6–8 weeks), legal sign-off on SLA credits, need for detailed region-by-region capacity plan, and confirmation of expected egress/cross-region cost model.
